result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.laplacian_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute Laplacian centrality for each node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L38816-L38885){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.laplacian_centrality( normalized=True, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Laplacian centrality](/assets/graphs/laplacian-centrality.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared seven-node graph shaded by Laplacian centrality, the share of the graph's Laplacian energy lost when a node is removed. Removing hub C costs the most, 0.24, then D 0.18, B and E 0.17, while the pendant node G costs only 0.03." width="100%"} Laplacian centrality measures how much the overall connectivity of the network is disrupted by removing a node. It uses a closed-form expression based on the Laplacian energy of the graph: $$\Delta E(v) = d(v)^2 + d(v) + 2 \sum_{u \in N(v)} d(u)$$ When normalized (the default), the score is divided by the total Laplacian energy of the graph, so values sum to `1.0`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (the default), normalize by total Laplacian energy so values sum to `1.0`. If `False`, return raw energy-drop values. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name for the node attribute to store results. If not provided, defaults to `"laplacian_centrality"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, return the raw dictionary. If `False`, store as node attributes and return self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to Laplacian centrality scores. Otherwise returns self. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a star graph, the hub contributes the most Laplacian energy: ::: {#c9b0742e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=False) g.add_nodes(["hub", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5"]) g.add_edges([("hub", "1"), ("hub", "2"), ("hub", "3"), ("hub", "4"), ("hub", "5")]) g.laplacian_centrality(return_dict=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {3: 0.12, 1: 0.4, 5: 0.12, 6: 0.12, 4: 0.12, 2: 0.12} ``` ::: :::
